chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about completing the prayer and fasting in the two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), so he said: 'Complete it, even if it is one prayer.'

key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: The two Sanctuaries (referring to Mecca and Medina)

ai.seo_question: Do travelers shorten their prayers when they are in Mecca or Medina?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the specific ruling for travelers within the boundaries of the two Sanctuaries, establishing that the concession of shortening prayers (qasr) is suspended in favor of full prayer (tamm). The phrase 'even if only one prayer' underscores the permanence of this status for the duration of the stay, distinguishing it from the temporary nature of travel elsewhere. This ruling is pivotal in Shia fiqh for determining the prayer status of those residing in or visiting Mecca and Medina.
